title: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck
description: Jemima wants a quiet place to hatch her eggs, but the charming gentleman who offers her a nest in the woods has plans of his own.
catalogueBlurb: Jemima finds a secret nest and a very suspicious new friend.

cover.alt: Beatrix Potter's original cover for The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck.

text.source: Original Story House retelling based on Beatrix Potter's public-domain 1908 story
text.notes: The underlying 1908 story is public domain in the UK and United States. This wording is an original child-friendly Unicorn Valley retelling.

illustrations.notes: The selected original Potter illustration files are identified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons.

rights.curatorNotes: Split into five short reader sections, preserving the cautionary shape of Potter's story while softening the harsher ending for the target reader. The Story House edition now offers independently selectable Classic and Modern illustration sets.

rights.notes: The selected original Potter illustration files are identified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons.

illustrations.alt: Jemima stands beside a discovered farm nest while the farmer's wife tends the eggs in the sunny farmyard.

illustrations.alt: Jemima flies from the farm hill towards the distant woodland, her blue bonnet and patterned shawl streaming behind her.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Jemima meets the sandy-whiskered fox beside a mossy stump, with his newspaper resting naturally on the stump.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The fox shows Jemima a tumble-down woodland shed filled with straw and loose feathers.

illustrations.alt: Jemima proudly stands beside exactly nine pale eggs in the feather-lined nest while the fox watches from the doorway.

illustrations.alt: Jemima listens as the fox makes his suspicious dinner invitation outside the feather shed.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Jemima carries a basket of herbs and two onions across the farm lane as Kep notices her unusual errand.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Jemima explains her secret nest and the fox to Kep on the farm lane, with the road towards the wood behind them.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Jemima steps back cautiously with her basket as the fox waits impatiently outside the feather shed.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Jemima and Kep stand safely by the shed while two other farm dogs chase the fox away through the woodland.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

text.source: Beatrix Potter's 1908 text, transcribed in Project Gutenberg eBook #14814
text.notes: Complete story text. Project Gutenberg header, footer, licence text and standalone [Illustration] placeholders are excluded; wording is not abridged, softened or modernised.

illustrations.source: Original 1908 illustrations by Beatrix Potter, Project Gutenberg eBook #14814
illustrations.notes: All 25 narrative illustrations appearing after the opening story text in the Project Gutenberg HTML edition are included in source order. Front-matter emblem/title artwork is excluded.

edition.notes: Story House pagination is presentation only; the original wording remains unabridged.

rights.curatorNotes: Complete original text reflowed into 10 reader pages at paragraph boundaries, with all 25 narrative illustrations from the Project Gutenberg 1908 edition restored at their matching passage anchors. The original, harsher ending is preserved in Full Classic Text.
